questions.title: Can a site belong to more than one department?
questions.ask: Two hundred and forty of your one thousand and thirty-two sites carry more than one department in the same field, separated by semicolons. Is that site genuinely shared, or does the first department named own it?
questions.why: Every table in this file is per department and every column has to add up to the bank-wide total. Counted under all three, the column totals more than the bank. Counted under the first, two departments are under-reported.
questions.good: A rule we can apply to all 240. First named owns it is a fine answer.
questions.fallback: If you cannot decide today, give us the list of 240 and we will bring back what each rule does to the numbers.
questions.unblocks: The correctness of every per-department figure in the report.

questions.title: Which SharePoint sites belong to which project?
questions.ask: We need a list: project number, project name, facility type, and the SharePoint site or sites for that project. Does that list exist, and who keeps it?
questions.why: Slides 36, 37 and 38 are three whole screens. Not one figure on any of them can be produced without this. We can count documents, records and users for any site. We cannot tell which sites are project sites.
questions.good: A named owner and a spreadsheet, even a one-off export.
questions.fallback: A one-off list unblocks the whole dashboard today. A maintained list keeps it correct. Start with the one-off.
questions.unblocks: The entire Project Insights dashboard, all 20 rows.

questions.title: Where is the register of EDRMS users?
questions.ask: Your own slide 54 asks this question and answers it with the exact table we need: name, staff or contractor or consultant, onboarded since go-live, training completed. Who owns that list, and can we have it?
questions.why: Microsoft 365 tells us who used SharePoint and when. It cannot tell us what kind of person they are, or whether they were trained. No system we can reach holds that.
questions.good: An owner, a location, and a refresh cycle.
questions.fallback: If there is no register, say so plainly and we will take those columns off both dashboards rather than leave them looking pending.
questions.unblocks: Five columns on Bank-wide and four on Department Insights.

questions.title: When did each site become EDRMS compliant?
questions.ask: Slide 53 puts Go-Live date at the top of every department screen. Is there a go-live date per department or per site, or may we use the site creation date instead?
questions.why: We checked every date column in the Cloud Governance export. Created Time is when the SharePoint site was created, which is not the same thing: sites made outside Cloud Governance are converted afterwards.
questions.good: Either a date list, or explicit agreement that creation date stands in.
questions.fallback: Agreement to use creation date is a perfectly good answer, but we need you to say it, so the caption can say it too.
questions.unblocks: Go-live on every department screen, and onboarded since go-live.

questions.title: What is a division, and what populates it?
questions.ask: Eight rows across two tabs ask for a per division breakdown. What is a division at ADB, and which system records which division a site, a person or a record belongs to?
questions.why: Nothing we can read carries it. Not SharePoint, not Cloud Governance, not the EDRMS database.
questions.good: A field in a named system, or a mapping list.
questions.fallback: If division is not recorded anywhere, we take those eight rows out rather than carry them as pending forever.
questions.unblocks: Four columns on Bank-wide, four on Department Insights.

questions.title: What records a physical record being turned over to RAC?
questions.ask: EDRMS tells us a declared record has a paper counterpart. What tells us that the paper actually reached RAC?
questions.why: Your completion rate needs both halves. We have the numerator source and not the denominator event. It is also the same gap as records awaiting transfer on the holdings dashboard.
questions.good: A system and a field, even a manual log.
questions.fallback: If nothing records it, that is itself the finding, and it belongs in the report as a gap rather than as a blank.
questions.unblocks: The counterpart completion rate, and the transfer figure on tab 6.

questions.title: The disposal fields: approver, status, disposed month on month
questions.ask: Slides 43 and 60 ask for a disposal approver, an approved, declined and extended status, and records disposed month on month. None of that is recorded in EDRMS today. Should it be, and who changes the application?
questions.why: This is a change request to the EDRMS application, not a reporting gap. We can report it the day it is captured, and not a day before.
questions.good: A yes or no on whether the application will capture it, and by when.
questions.fallback: If it is not going to be captured, we remove eleven rows across two tabs today.
questions.unblocks: Seven rows on Bank-wide, six on Department Insights, one on tab 5.

questions.title: Month on month figures: do you want them, and how far back?
questions.ask: Several slides ask for a month on month indicator. Microsoft 365 usage reports only reach back 180 days. Is a rolling 180 days enough, or do you need history from go-live?
questions.why: If you need history, we have to start snapshotting now, because the window closes behind us every day.
questions.good: A number of months, and a decision on whether we start snapshotting.
questions.fallback: If undecided, we start snapshotting anyway. It costs little and the data cannot be recovered later.
questions.unblocks: Every month on month indicator in the report.

questions.title: Visitors: internal, external, and access requests
questions.ask: Slide 56 asks for visitors split internal and external, and for access requests granted and denied. Which report should we read for that split, and where do access requests live?
questions.why: The usage report gives us page views and visited pages per site. It does not label a visitor internal or external, and it says nothing about access requests.
questions.good: A named report or a named system.
questions.fallback: If neither exists, we take the four rows off slide 56.

questions.title: Departmental libraries: the picker, and users per library
questions.ask: Slides 61 to 66 give each file plan category its own screen. Do you want a picker across the six categories, and do you need the number of users per library?
questions.why: The picker is a build decision we can make today. Users per library needs a per library permission read that nothing currently produces.
questions.good: Yes or no on the picker. For users per library, an acknowledgement that it needs a new source.
questions.fallback: Picker yes, users per library parked.

questions.title: Which retention labels are permanent and which are temporary?
questions.ask: The whole of tab 5 splits on permanent against temporary. Which of your Purview retention labels fall on each side?
questions.why: We can read the labels. We cannot infer which are permanent, and guessing puts records on the wrong side of a disposal decision.
questions.good: A list of label names against the two categories.
questions.fallback: If the labels are still being designed, tell us when they settle.
questions.unblocks: The split behind every figure on tab 5.

questions.title: Where does the Institutional File Plan live, and who maintains it?
questions.ask: Tab 4 is built from the term store. Is the term store the file plan of record, and who is allowed to change it?
questions.why: If the authoritative file plan is a document somewhere and the term store is a copy, then this dashboard reports the copy.
questions.good: A named system and a named owner.
questions.fallback: If it is a document, we need it, and a cycle for refreshing it.
questions.unblocks: The authority of every figure on tab 4.

questions.title: How do we know which library or document uses which term?
questions.ask: Every per term figure needs a link from the term to the library or the document. Is the term applied as a managed metadata column, and is it mandatory?
questions.why: If it is optional, the per term counts under-report by exactly as much as people skip it, and the report has to say so.
questions.good: Mandatory, optional, or applied at library level only.
questions.fallback: Whatever the answer, we caption it. An optional field reported as complete is the worst outcome.
questions.unblocks: Six rows on tab 4, and the honesty of the rest.

questions.title: New library and new term requests: are they tracked?
questions.ask: Slides 48 to 52 ask for requests for new libraries and new terms. Are those requests raised in a system, or by email?
questions.why: If they are raised in Cloud Governance we can count them tomorrow. If they are email, nobody can count them.
questions.fallback: If email, we say so on the screen rather than showing a zero.

questions.title: Is eServe the retrieval system of record, and who owns it?
questions.ask: Your slide 67 says retrieval is processed from eServe. eServe has never been connected to this project. Is it the system of record for storage and retrieval requests, and who owns it?
questions.why: Every figure on tab 6 is currently an illustration built from the totals you printed on slide 67. eServe is what would make them real.
questions.good: Yes or no, plus an owner and whether an extract is possible.
questions.fallback: If eServe cannot be reached, ask whether RAC keeps its own register, in any form, even a spreadsheet.

questions.title: Can room capacity be included, and does retrieval free it up?
questions.ask: Your slide 68 asks us whether room capacity and percentage available storage can be included. Your slide 69 asks whether retrieval frees it up again. Both are questions you put to us. We are putting them back: is capacity per location recorded anywhere, and what counts as full?
questions.why: We drew a capacity chart once, with invented percentages, and took it out on the 24th precisely because it answered your question with a guess.
questions.good: A capacity figure per location and a definition of full.
questions.fallback: If capacity is not recorded, we drop both, and you have your answer.
questions.unblocks: Two open questions on tab 6, and a chart that can then be drawn.

questions.title: What should the Records and Archive Holdings dashboard actually be?
questions.ask: Tab 6 is built to the shape of your slides 67, 68 and 69, with your own published totals. Is that the dashboard you want, or is it a screenshot of a system you want us to replace?
questions.why: This is the one dashboard where we are not sure whether we are building a report or duplicating an existing one.
questions.good: A clear statement of what this screen is for, and who reads it.
questions.fallback: If it is a duplicate, say so and we will scope it down to the one figure that is genuinely ours.
